sentences.text: The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No574/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tirur is the appellant herein.
((For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are 2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 27.9.2012.

According to the petitioner, on 27.9.2012. at about 2.30 p.m., while he was travelling in a motor cycle, he was hit down by a lorry bearing registration No.KL-45-9177 driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner and as a result of which, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2 nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver 2025:KER:10001 of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs6,36,200/- limited to Rs.6,36,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A23.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,78,500/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9. Heard Sri. A.N. Santhosh, the learned Counsel appearing for 2025:KER:10001 the petitioner/appellant,
Though notice was served, nobody turned up for the respondents.

sentences.text: 10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was a student of Civil Engineering Diploma course, but the Tribunal has not awarded any loss of disability on the ground that he was only a student.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2012 will come to Rs.8500/- Therefore, the petitioner being a student of Civil Engineering Diploma course, his notional income is fixed at Rs.10,000/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of disability.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"fracture to right tibia, fracture to fibula, 5x5 cm 2025:KER:10001 contaminated lacerated wound over the anterior aspect of middle third, multiple lacerated wound above right leg, superficial abrasions over the right elbow, wound debridement and external stabilization right tibia, wound debridement and vac application under spinal anesthesia and transposition flop cover and skin grafting for the raw area under regional anesthesia."
13. According to the learned counsel, before the Tribunal, an application was filed for referring the petitioner to a Medical Board.
Though the said application was allowed, before receiving the disability certificate, the Tribunal disposed of the matter.
He has also produced a copy of the disability certificate,
It is marked as Ext. A23.
The medical board has assessed the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as 20%.
I do not find any ground to disbelieve Ext.A23 and hence the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed at 20%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 21 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v 2025:KER:10001 Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.6,04,800/-.
15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.5,000/- was awarded and towards 'transportation expenses' Rs.7,500/- was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
16. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 44 days and as outpatient on 18 times.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life' and 'transportation expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.50,000/-,

4 Damage to clothing etc. 1,000/- 1,000/-

 7 Loss of disability Nil 6,04,800/-
 Loss of Education 20,000/- 20,000/-

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.9,35,800/- (Rupees Nine Lakh Thirty Five Thousand and Eight Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the 2025:KER:10001 Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
21.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
